headline: Yale police firearm discharges during New Haven rescue attempt, officials say
dek: The weapon did not strike the person inside the locked car, who was critically hurt while self-harming; Connecticut’s inspector general is investigating the response.
body: A Yale police officer’s firearm discharged Wednesday morning while the officer was trying to reach a person who was self-harming inside a locked car in New Haven, according to Yale officials, Mayor Justin Elicker and separate local television reports. The person was not hit by the gunfire but was taken to Yale New Haven Hospital in critical condition with injuries described by officials as self-inflicted.

The incident unfolded at about 9:21 a.m. in the New Haven Yale Club parking lot behind 205 Whitney Avenue, Elicker told [NBC Connecticut](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/yale/3784890/). Yale police responded after receiving a report involving a person inside the vehicle. A Yale alert issued around 9:40 a.m. said there was no threat to the wider community, according to [Patch](https://patch.com/connecticut/newhaven/new-haven-police-investigating-incident-205-whitney-avenue-street-closed-yale).

Duane Lovello, Yale’s head of public safety, said in a statement that the officer saw the person attempting to harm themselves and tried to intervene. The vehicle was locked. As the officer attempted to break the window with the firearm, the weapon discharged, Lovello said. After the person was removed, the officer began medical aid before emergency medical personnel arrived, according to the account reported by NBC Connecticut and [WFSB](https://www.wfsb.com/2026/10/14/police-investigate-scene-whitney-avenue-new-haven/).

The available reporting does not establish precisely how the weapon discharged or whether the firearm contacted the glass before firing. It does establish that the person inside the vehicle was not struck by the round. Elicker said the person appeared to be stabbing themselves when the officer arrived, and NBC Connecticut reported that surgery was underway Wednesday morning. The person’s identity and further medical details were not released.

The responding Yale officer was also undergoing a medical evaluation, Lovello said. The New Haven Police Department and Yale Police Department were assisting at the scene, while Connecticut’s Office of the State Inspector General took over the investigation. WFSB reported that the inspector general’s involvement is required when a police officer discharges a weapon in a use-of-force incident, and that body-worn-camera video was expected to be released in the following days.

Whitney Avenue was closed between Sachem Street and Humphrey Street while investigators worked near the Yale Club, affecting traffic and access to nearby buildings. Yale’s initial public alert asked people to avoid the area, but the reports did not describe an ongoing threat to students, employees or residents. The closure and response also led the mayor to cancel a scheduled briefing about the Lower State Street Redesign Project, according to Patch.

The episode raises two separate questions that remain unresolved: what led the person to the vehicle and exactly how the officer’s firearm discharged during the rescue attempt. Those questions are now part of the inspector general’s review, and the initial accounts do not announce any finding of wrongdoing. The investigation is also expected to clarify the officer’s actions, the timing of the medical response and what the camera footage shows.

For New Haven, the incident is both a public-safety investigation and a mental-health emergency response that happened in a busy area near Yale’s campus. Yale said it was thinking of everyone involved as they received medical care. NBC Connecticut also included information for people in crisis: anyone who may be at immediate risk can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. No additional details about the patient, the officer or the investigation had been released by Wednesday evening.
